beats.narration_text: The obvious guess is that practicing IRAC with Claude means Claude hands you the finished IRAC — the model answer, cleanly written, ready to copy. Wrong branch. It's drilling you through Issue, Rule, Application, one step at a time. So: what does that drill actually make you do?

beats.narration_text: A Skill isn't a plugin or a hidden LLM behavior — it's a folder. This one is called irac-practice, and inside it is a single file, SKILL.md, written in plain English. That file is the whole program: the drill order, when to wait for you, what to check, what earns credit. The choice is deliberate — text you can read is text you can audit. No hidden logic sitting where the student can't see it.

The drill lives in a Steps section — a numbered list Claude runs top to bottom. Pose the hypo, then wait: your Issue first, then your Rule, then your Application, in that order, before checking anything. Linear — no branching, no jumping ahead, unless a step itself says otherwise. What that buys you is the whole point of IRAC — you build the analysis in order, instead of leaping to the answer that felt right and reverse-engineering the reasoning.

production_viz.label: POSE, PAUSE, CHECK
production_viz.caption: linear — no skipping ahead unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: One check inside the drill is specific and unforgiving: state the right Conclusion without showing the Application and you've earned nothing. Here's what's actually happening — the Application is where the Rule meets the facts, one fact at a time, and that mapping is the whole intellectual move IRAC exists to force. Skip it and the Conclusion is a guess wearing the right answer. The Skill treats that gap as the point. It's optimizing for the habit that survives after the video ends: reasoning shown, not conclusions guessed.

production_viz.label: CONCLUSION, OR APPLICATION
production_viz.caption: only the Application actually earns credit

beats.narration_text: Claude isn't grading your Conclusion — it's checking whether you showed the Application, one fact at a time, on the way to it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: I want to practice IRAC on law-school hypos. Here's a hypo — paste it in. Don't hand me the model answer. Drill me: ask for my Issue first and wait. Then ask for my Rule and wait. Then ask for my Application, walking me through the facts one at a time. Only check my Conclusion after I've given all three, and if I try to jump ahead, refuse and send me back to whichever step I skipped. Go deeper: ask the same model to write you three hypos where the tempting answer is wrong because one specific fact changes how the Rule applies — and name the fact in each one.

llm_exercise.prompt: I want to practice IRAC on law-school hypos. Here's a hypo: [paste your hypo]. Don't hand me the model answer. Drill me: (1) ask for my Issue first and wait for my response. (2) Then ask for my Rule and wait. (3) Then ask for my Application, walking me through the facts one at a time. (4) Only check my Conclusion after I've given all three. If I try to jump ahead to the Conclusion, refuse and send me back to whichever step I skipped. When you check my Application, tell me which specific fact I mapped well and which I glossed over.
